title: Groundwater hydrology and chemistry in and near an emulsified vegetable-oil injection zone, Solid Waste Management Unit 17, Naval Weapons Station Charleston, North Charleston, South Carolina, 2004-2009
citation: Vroblesky, D.A., Petkewich, M.D., Lowery, M.A., Conlon, K.J., and Casey, C.C., 2010, Groundwater hydrology and chemistry in and near an emulsified vegetable-oil injection zone, Solid Waste Management Unit 17, Naval Weapons Station Charleston, North Charleston, South Carolina, 2004-2009: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report SIR-2009-5239, map scale 1:2,940.
notes:
SWMU17 groundwater report. Site geology on p. 19 is quoted by the authors from Tetra Tech NUS (2006) and Borden and others (2008); recorded as informal lithologic units without formal names. Table 2 (p. 17) wells recorded with northing/easting, total depth and screen interval; the ground elevation is chosen as the lower of the two elevation columns (inferred). Not recorded: VOC concentrations (table 3), water-quality parameters (table 4), pH-adjustment test chronology (table 1), and water-table elevations on map figures 7-9 and 11 (labels not reliably paired with wells). The last part of p. 30 continues into the next packet.
Pages 31-36: discussion of the dechlorination stall, table 5 (molecular microbiology; not recorded), VOC trends (not recorded) and summary. Recorded the reported permeability reduction in the injection zone. Pages 39-41: Appendix 1 and 2 water levels (about 180 readings of depth to water and water level above NAVD 88; not recorded individually). The appendix 'Datum' column (e.g. 7.78 ft for 16MW-01S) matches the higher of the two elevation columns of table 2, which supports reading the lower table 2 value as ground elevation in packet-01. References (pp. 37-38): recorded the SC site reports and SWMU17/NWS Charleston papers; skipped general microbiology, chemistry and sampling-method references (Barcelona, Bradley, Cirpka, Cupples, Dennis, Fennell, He, Hendrickson, Holliger, Looney, McMahon, Sevee, Shanklin, Vroblesky 1996, Wiedemeier, Zhuang).
